objective: Prevent duplicate heavy-worker launches when client/tool transport times out, retries, disconnects, or the bootstrap process dies while the worker remains alive.

required_for: heavy jobs whose runtime can exceed one client/tool request
development backtests and parity jobs when launched from chat/runtime surfaces
other transactional jobs with expensive non-idempotent or storage-heavy execution

mandatory_invariants: A client/tool timeout is transport state only and MUST NOT be interpreted as worker failure.
Each job is identified by job_id plus canonical job-spec SHA-256 and an atomic claim_token.
A retry MUST inspect durable claim, process identity, receipt and artifacts before any relaunch.
A live bootstrap with exact PID plus process-birth identity MUST be adopted and MUST NOT be relaunched.
If bootstrap is dead but its worker is alive with exact PID plus process-birth identity, the worker MUST be adopted as ADOPT_ORPHAN_WORKER and MUST NOT be relaunched.
PID alone is never proof of process identity; process birth identity is mandatory.
Linux zombie processes are dead for liveness purposes and MUST NOT block receipt promotion.
An active attempt directory MUST NEVER be deleted or replaced by a retry.
A failed attempt is archived immutably before any permitted retry.
Relaunch is allowed only after positive proof that neither bootstrap nor worker of the current claim is alive and no valid completed receipt can be promoted.
Default max_attempts is 2: one initial launch plus at most one proven-death retry.
Capsule/spec drift for an existing job_id MUST fail closed.
Receipt promotion requires exact expected fields and exact artifact byte sizes plus SHA-256.
Promotion to done is atomic and only occurs after the worker is no longer live.
A receipt written before process exit MUST NOT be promoted while the worker/bootstrap is still live.
Unsafe job_id/path traversal MUST fail closed.
A live controller lock MUST NOT be stolen because of wall-clock age.
If process-birth identity cannot be established on the current OS/runtime, execution MUST fail closed rather than guess liveness.
One expensive scientific unit must be durably validated and persisted before the next expensive unit begins.

legacy.reason: It uses blocking subprocess.run and deletes prior temporary directories before proving that a prior worker is dead; therefore it is not authorized for transport-resilient heavy execution.
